newsitem.title: USA: Japan PM hails Japan-US ties amid trade concern.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM hails Japan-US ties amid trade concern.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Monday applauded the close overall relationship between Japan and the United States but the optimism could be tempered by U.S. concern about Tokyo's surging trade surplus.
President Bill Clinton on Sunday warned Japan that it risked an economic war with the United States if its trade surplus started exploding again.

In a speech delivered to 300 business executives, academics and students at Columbia University, Hashimoto stressed that a change in Japan's economic and trading structures will help cut Tokyo's trade surplus.

"Because of such a structural change, the mid- and long-term trend in Japan's trade surplus with the United States is on the decrease," he said. "This should have a positive influence on Japan-U.S. economic relations over the coming years."

Japan last week reported that its overall trade surplus more than tripled in May to $6.53 billion from a year earlier after doubling in April. The surplus with the United States alone surged 93 percent in May to $2.85 billion.
Hashimoto's remarks followed a harsh statement by Clinton that was made at a press conference after a Group of Seven summit on Sunday.
"If we return to a time when we've got exploding trade deficits then that will once again move front and centre into our relationship in a way that won't be good for either country," he said.
U.S. officials are worried that the current rise is the start of a steady climb in the surplus back to levels that in the past have led to trade friction.
Hashimoto tried to dispel any worries about U.S.-Japan relations by stressing the magnitude of the contribution that Japanese direct investment has been making to the U.S. economy.

"In recent years, Japanese companies, particularly those in the manufacturing sector, are increasingly transferring their production capacity abroad; and in the U.S. this has created 730,000 new jobs," he said.
Hashimoto, wrapping up his U.S. visit on Tuesday, noted that Japan-U.S. relations are important not only for the two countries but also for the rest of the world.
"I am convinced that even in the 21st century the Japan- U.S. partnership should be able to bring about the fruits of stability and prosperity to our two peoples," he added.
Hashimoto is due to leave for Europe on Tuesday for talks with heads of the European Union and for his first summit with leaders of Scandinavian countries.
